Σταυρὸς, χειμαζομένων λιμὴν εὐδιέστατος. Σταυρὸς, πολεμουμένων εἰρήνη
ἀστασίαστος. Σταυρὸς, ὀρθο δόξων καύχημα καυχημάτων, καὶ αἱρετικῶν κατά κριμα
ἀκατάπαυστον. 4085Σταυρὸς, εἰδωλολατρείας κατάλυσις καὶ εὐσεβείας ἀνόρθωσις.
Σταυρὸς, παρθενίας διδάσκαλος καὶ σωφροσύνης φύλαξ. Σταυρὸς, δικαίων ἀσφάλεια
καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν μετάνοια. Σταυρὸς, μοναζόντων ἐγκαλλώπισμα καὶ σεμνῶς
βιούντων εὐκοσμία.Σταυρὸς, νηπίων φύλαξ, καὶ νέων σωφρονισμὸς, καὶ γερόντων
στηριγμοῦ βακτηρία. Σταυρὸς, πτωχῶν ἀδαπάνητος θησαυρὸς, καὶ πλουσίων
αὐταρκείας διδάσκαλος. Σταυρὸς, πεπλανημένων ὁδὸς, καὶ ἀπολλυμένων ἀπλανὴς
ὁδηγός. Σταυρὸς, ἀνάπαυσις ἐν κόποις ἡμερινοῖς, καὶ βοήθεια ἐν φόβοις νυκτε
ρινοῖς. Σταυρὸς, ἐθνῶν εὐταξία, καὶ παντὸς τοῦ κόσμου βαθυτάτη γαλήνη.Καὶ τί
εἴπωμεν, ἢ τί παραλείψωμεν, ἢ πῶς σε ἀνυμνήσωμεν, πανένδοξε σταυρέ; ὅτι σὲ
μόνον ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς κτίσεως ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης ἀνέδειξεν ὅπλον ἀήττητον κατὰ
τοῦ διαβόλου, καὶ τῆς ἁμαρ τίας, καὶ τοῦ θανάτου. ∆ιὸ μακάριοί ἐσμεν πάντες οἱ
καταξιωθέντες τὴν ἁγίαν ἰδεῖν ἡμέραν τῆς σῆς ἀναδείξεως. Σὺ εἶ τῶν προφητῶν τὸ
κήρυγμα· περὶ σοῦ γὰρ ἀγαλλιώμενοι ὁσημέραι κελαδοῦσι λέγοντες πρὸς τὸν Θεόν·
«Ἔδωκας τοῖς φοβουμένοις σε σημείωσιν τοῦ φυγεῖν ἀπὸ προσώπου τόξου.» Σὺ εἶ τὸ
καύχημα τῶν ἀποστόλων. Ἀδιαλείπτως γὰρ βοῶσιν ἐν Ἐκκλησίᾳ ἁγίᾳ δι' ἑνὸς
αὐτῶν ἱεροκήρυκος· «Ἐμοὶ δὲ μὴ γένοιτο καυχᾶσθαι, εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ Κυρίου
ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. «Σὺ εἶ καὶ τῶν μαρτύρων στέφανος· ἐπειδὴ καὶ αὐτοὶ τὸν
σταυρὸν ἄραντες ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Κυρίῳ. Σὺ εἶ τὸ καύχημα καὶ τὸ ἀγαλλίαμα τῶν
ἐν ὅρεσι καὶ σπηλαίοις καὶ ταῖς ὀπαῖς τῆς γῆς κατοικούντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ
Κυρίου· ὅτι καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν σάρκα ἐσταύρωσαν σὺν τοῖς παθήμασι καὶ ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις.
Σὺ τῶν ἐγγὺς καὶ τῶν μακρὰν ἀναψυχὴ καὶ ἀνάπαυσις. Ὢ τῆς ἀνεκλαλήτου χάριτος
τοῦ ∆εσποτικοῦ σταυροῦ! Ὢ τῶν ἐν αὐτῷ ἀνεκλαλήτων καὶ ἀκαταλήπτων
μυστηρίων!Καὶ ἵν' εἴπω κἀγὼ ἐκστατικόν τι μετὰ τῆς ἱερᾶς σάλπιγγος· «Ὦ βάθος
πλούτου καὶ σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως Θεοῦ, ὡς ἀνεξερεύνητα τὰ κρίματα αὐτοῦ!» Παρὰ
γὰρ τῷ ξύλῳ τῆς ζωῆς νεκρωθέντες, παρὰ τῷ ξύλῳ τῆς κατακρίσεως
ἐζωοποιήθημεν. ∆ιὰ τὴν ἄμετρον χάριν τοῦ σεσωκότος ∆εσπότου δέον ἡμᾶς τὴν
πανέορτον ταύτην συστήσασθαι «ἐν τοῖς πυκάζουσιν ἕως τῶν κεράτων τοῦ
θυσιαστηρίου.» Πυκάζοντα δέ εἰσιν, ὥς φασιν οἱ περὶ ταῦτα δεινοὶ, τὰ ἐξ ἀμελείας ἢ
παλαιότητος ῥυπωθέντα, εἶτα ἐξ ἐπιμελείας καὶ σπουδῆς πάλιν ἐπὶ τὸ
τιμαλφέστερον μετακοσμούμενα εἰς εὐφροσύνην καὶ τέρψιν τῶν εὐωχηθησομένων
ἐν γάμοις ἐν ἑτέρᾳ τινὶ φαιδρᾷ θυμηδίᾳ. ∆ιατεθῶμεν τοίνυν ὡς προτετάγμεθα, καὶ
τὴν συμβᾶσαν ἡμῶν ἐκ ῥᾳθυμίας τῷ συνειδότι ἀπεκδυσάμενοι ἀειδίαν, τὴν φαιδρὰν
ταύτην καὶ πάνσεπτον ἡμέραν τῆς τοῦ ζωοποιοῦ σταυροῦ μνήμης ἐπιτελέσωμεν,
ἐλεημοσύναις τε καὶ πίστει, καθώς φησιν ἡ θεία Γραφὴ, παῤῥησίαν ἐν εὐλαβείᾳ
κεκοσμημένην4088 ἀναλαβόντες, καὶ ἄραντες ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων τὸ νικητικὸν ὅπλον
τοῦ ζωοποιοῦ σταυροῦ, τὸν δωρηθέντα ἡμῖν οὐρανόθεν εἰς παῦσιν πάσης ὀργῆς
ἀγγελικὸν ὕμνον συνήθως πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν βοήσωμεν· «Ἅγιος ὁ Θεὸς, ἅγιος ἰσχυρὸς,
ἅγιος ἀθάνατος, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς·» ἁγία Τριὰς, ἀκατάληπτε, ἀπεριόριστε, ἀνεκφοίτητε,
ὁμοούσιε, καὶ ὁμόθρονε, καὶ ὁμόχρονε, καὶ ὁμόδοξε, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς, καὶ ἱλάσθητι ταῖς
ἁμαρτίαις ἡμῶν ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός σου τοῦ ἁγίου, καὶ δὸς ἡμῖν εὑρεῖν ἔλεος καὶ
οἰκτιρμοὺς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς ἀνταποδόσεώς σου τῆς δικαίας. Σὺ γὰρ εἶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν,
καὶ πρέπει σοι τῷ Πατρὶ, καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ, καὶ τῷ Πνεύματι δόξα, μεγαλοσύνη, κράτος καὶ
ἐξουσία πρὸ παντὸς αἰῶνος, καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς τοὺς σύμπαντας αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
Ἀμήν.

thought_title: Closing litany of the Cross and doxological prayer
orientation: The narrator is closing the encomium with a long series of praises of the Cross, then turns to direct address and a final prayer to the Trinity.
pass_a_gloss: Cross, a most calm harbor for the storm-tossed. Cross, an unshaken peace for those at war. Cross, a boast of boasts for the orthodox, and an unceasing condemnation for heretics. Cross, a destruction of idolatry and a raising up of piety. Cross, a teacher of virginity and a guardian of self-control. Cross, a security for the righteous and a repentance for sinners. Cross, an adornment for monks and a good order for those living reverently. Cross, a guardian of infants, and a discipline of the young, and a staff of support for the old. Cross, a treasure without cost for the poor, and a teacher of self-sufficiency for the rich. Cross, a road for the straying, and an unerring guide for the perishing. Cross, a rest in daytime labors, and a help in nighttime fears. Cross, a good order of nations, and a deepest calm of the whole world. And what shall we say, or what shall we pass over, or how shall we hymn you, all-glorious Cross? Because you alone from all creation the King of glory showed forth as an unconquered weapon against the devil, and against sin, and against death. Therefore blessed are we all who were deemed worthy to see the holy day of your exaltation. You are the proclamation of the prophets; for rejoicing over you daily they sing out, saying to God: "You gave to those who fear you a sign to flee from the face of the bow." You are the boast of the apostles. For unceasingly they cry out in the holy Church through one of them, a sacred herald: "But may it never be for me to boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." You are also the crown of the martyrs; since they too, having taken up the cross, followed the Lord. You are the boast and the exultation of those dwelling in mountains and caves and the holes of the earth for the name of the Lord; because they too crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. You are a refreshment and a rest for those near and those far. O the inexpressible grace of the Master's cross! O the inexpressible and incomprehensible mysteries in it! And so that I too may say something ecstatic with the sacred trumpet: "O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God, how unsearchable are his judgments!" For having been put to death by the tree of condemnation, we were made alive by the tree of life. Because of the immeasurable grace of the Master who saved us, it is necessary for us to establish this all-festal day "among the thick branches up to the horns of the altar." And adorning things are, as those skilled in these matters say, the things soiled from neglect or old age, then again from care and diligence transformed to the more precious for the gladness and delight of those who will feast at weddings in some other bright merriment. Let us therefore be disposed as we have been instructed, and having stripped off the unseemliness that has befallen our conscience from laziness, let us celebrate this bright and all-revered day of the memory of the life-giving cross, with almsgiving and faith, as the divine Scripture says, having taken up boldness adorned with reverence, and having lifted upon our shoulders the victorious weapon of the life-giving cross, let us cry out to God the angelic hymn given to us from heaven for the ceasing of all wrath, as is customary: "Holy God, holy mighty, holy immortal, have mercy on us;" holy Trinity, incomprehensible, unbounded, inseparable, one in being, and sharing one throne, and sharing one time, and sharing one glory, have mercy on us, and be merciful to our sins for the sake of your holy name, and grant us to find mercy and compassion in the day of your righteous recompense. For you are our God, and to you, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, belong glory, majesty, might and authority before every age, and now and to all the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: Superlative of εὔδιος, 'calm, fair weather'; 'most calm' keeps the superlative force for a harbor metaphor.
The alpha-privative of στασιάζω means 'without faction or civil strife'; 'unshaken' conveys stability in the context of peace for those at war.
The noun means a judicial sentence against someone; 'condemnation' preserves the legal force against heretics.
The noun from ἀνορθόω means 'setting upright again, restoration'; 'raising up' keeps the physical metaphor paired with 'destruction' of idolatry.
The alpha-privative of δαπανάω means 'not spent, not costing'; 'without cost' fits the paradox of a treasure for the poor.
The aorist of ἀναδείκνυμι means 'proclaimed, displayed publicly'; 'showed forth' links to the feast of the exaltation (ἀνάδειξις) in the brief.

pass_b_english: For those who are storm-tossed, the Cross is a harbor of perfect calm. For those who are attacked in war, the Cross is a peace that cannot be shaken. The Cross is the boast of boasts for the orthodox, and for heretics a condemnation that never rests. The Cross is the destruction of idolatry and the raising up of true reverence. The Cross is the teacher of virginity and the guardian of self-control. The Cross is the security of the righteous and the repentance of sinners. The Cross is the adornment of monks and the good order of those who live in holiness. The Cross is the protector of infants, the discipline of the young, and the supporting staff of the aged. The Cross is a treasure for the poor that costs nothing, and a teacher of self-sufficiency for the rich. The Cross is the road for those who have wandered, and an unerring guide for those who are perishing. The Cross is rest in the labors of the day, and help in the terrors of the night. The Cross is the good order of the nations, and the deepest calm of the whole world.

And what shall we say, or what shall we pass over, or how shall we praise you, all-glorious Cross? For the King of glory has shown you forth alone from all creation as an unconquered weapon against the devil, and against sin, and against death. Therefore we are all blessed who have been deemed worthy to see the holy day of your manifestation. You are the proclamation of the prophets; for rejoicing in you they sing out daily to God, saying: "You have given to those who fear you a banner by which to flee from before the bow" (Psalm 59:6 LXX; 60:4 in English Bibles). You are the boast of the apostles. For they cry out unceasingly in the holy Church through one of their sacred heralds: "May it never be for me to boast, except in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ" (Galatians 6:14). You are also the crown of the martyrs, since they too took up the Cross and followed the Lord. You are the boast and the joy of those who dwell in mountains and caves and holes in the earth for the name of the Lord, because they too have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. You are refreshment and rest for those near and those far off. O the inexpressible grace of the Master's Cross! O the inexpressible and incomprehensible mysteries in it!

And so that I too may say something inspired with the sacred trumpet: "O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments!" (Romans 11:33). For by the tree of life we were put to death, and by the tree of condemnation we were made alive. Because of the boundless grace of the Master who saved us, we must keep this all-festal feast "among the thick branches, up to the horns of the altar" (Psalm 118:27, LXX 117:27, following the Septuagint). Branches, as biblical interpreters say, are things that have been soiled by neglect or age, and then by care and diligence are adorned again to something more precious, for the gladness and delight of those who will feast at weddings in some other bright celebration. Let us therefore dispose ourselves as we have been instructed, and having stripped off the shame that has come upon our conscience from carelessness, let us celebrate this bright and all-holy day of the memory of the life-giving Cross with acts of mercy and with faith, taking up, as the divine Scripture says, a confidence adorned with reverence, and lifting on our shoulders the victorious weapon of the life-giving Cross, let us cry out to God the angelic hymn given to us from heaven for the ceasing of all wrath, as is our custom: "Holy God, holy mighty, holy immortal, have mercy on us." Holy Trinity, incomprehensible, unbounded, inseparable, one in being, sharing one throne, co-eternal, sharing one glory, have mercy on us, and be merciful to our sins for the sake of your holy name, and grant us to find mercy and compassion on the day of your just recompense. For you are our God, and to you, Father, Son, and Spirit, belong glory, majesty, might, and authority before every age, now and to all the ages of ages. Amen.
notes: The source has OCR damage at 'ὀρθο δόξων' (split across a line break) and 'ἁμαρ τίας' (split across a line break); both are restored as ὀρθοδόξων and ἁμαρτίας.
The source has a stray numeral '4085' before Σταυρὸς, εἰδωλολατρείας and '4088' after κεκοσμημένην; these are page or line numbers from the manuscript and are not translated.
The source has 'παῤῥησίαν' with a rough breathing mark; the standard form is παρρησίαν.
The source has 'ἀνεκφοίτητε' which is a rare form; the sense is 'not going out, inseparable' and is rendered 'inseparable'.

problems.quote: when we were put to death by the tree of life, we were made alive by the tree of condemnation
problems.source_quote: Παρὰ γὰρ τῷ ξύλῳ τῆς ζωῆς νεκρωθέντες, παρὰ τῷ ξύλῳ τῆς κατακρίσεως ἐζωοποιήθημεν
problems.why: Sense reversed: 'tree of life' should be 'tree of condemnation/death' and vice versa.
problems.fix: For by the tree of condemnation we were put to death, and by the tree of life we were made alive.

problems.quote: with branches, up to the horns of the altar
problems.source_quote: ἐν τοῖς πυκάζουσιν ἕως τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου
problems.why: πυκάζουσιν is a noun 'those who bind/fold' or 'compact companies,' not 'branches.'
problems.fix: with those who bind [the sacrifice], up to the horns of the altar
problems.ruling: πυκάζουσιν means 'dense crowds/thickets,' not 'branches'; author explicitly glosses it, so 'branches' misleads.

edits.new: For by the tree of condemnation we were put to death, and by the tree of life we were made alive.

problems.why: 'sharing one time' misrepresents ὁμόχρονε; with ὁμοούσιε and ὁμόθρονε, this means 'co-eternal' or 'of the same age/eternity', not 'sharing one time'
problems.fix: co-eternal
problems.ruling: ὁμόχρονε means co-eternal; 'sharing one time' is misleading alongside ὁμοούσιε and ὁμόθρονε.

edits.old: For by the tree of condemnation we were put to death, and by the tree of life we were made alive.
edits.new: For by the tree of life we were put to death, and by the tree of condemnation we were made alive.

πυκάζουσιν rendered as deck the feast, matching the context's definition of πυκάζοντα as things adorned.

problems.quote: with those who deck the feast, up to the horns of the altar
problems.source_quote: ἐν τοῖς πυκάζουσιν ἕως τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου

problems.fix: among the thick branches, up to the horns of the altar
problems.ruling: πυκάζουσιν is dative plural of πυκάζω ('to entwine, cover thickly'), not 'those who deck the feast'; 'branches' in next sentence confirms image of thick branches entwined around altar horns.

problems.quote: the life-giving Cross
problems.why: Many epithets for Cross may confuse reader about whether different objects are meant.
problems.fix: Note in intro that author uses varied epithets for same Cross.

variants.text: the life-giving wood of the glorious Cross
the victorious weapon of the life-giving Cross

problems.quote: And so that I too may say something ecstatic with the sacred trumpet
problems.why: Unclear who 'I' is—author Alexander, or persona? Breaks narrative frame suddenly.
problems.fix: Clarify this is author speaking in own voice.

problems.quote: as those skilled in these matters say
problems.why: Unidentified authorities; reader can't tell if this is Scripture, Fathers, or general learned opinion.
problems.fix: Identify as 'biblical interpreters' or similar.

problems.quote: Branches, as those skilled in these matters say, are things that have been soiled by neglect or age, and then by care and diligence are adorned again to something more precious
problems.why: Etymology seems forced; 'branches' (Greek kladoi?) may not mean this. Connection to Psalm 118:27 'bind the festal procession with branches' is strained.
problems.fix: Check Greek; may need note that this is allegorical interpretation.

problems.quote: a boldness adorned with reverence
problems.why: Oxymoronic: 'boldness' and 'reverence' clash awkwardly; likely 'confidence' or 'freedom' (Greek parrhesia).
problems.fix: Use 'confidence' or 'holy boldness.'

problems.quote: "You have given to those who fear you a sign by which to flee from before the bow" (Psalm 60:4 (LXX 60:4))
problems.why: Hebrew Psalm 60:4 reads 'you have given a banner to those who fear you, that it may be displayed because of the truth' (or 'to rally to'). 'Flee from before the bow' is LXX reading but obscure; check if quoted accurately.
problems.fix: Verify LXX text; current English seems to follow LXX closely but may confuse readers expecting Hebrew-based translations.

problems.quote: "among the thick branches, up to the horns of the altar" (Psalm 118:27, LXX 117:27)
problems.why: Hebrew Psalm 118:27 has 'bind the festal sacrifice with cords, up to the horns of the altar.' 'Thick branches' follows LXX 'kladoi' but changes meaning significantly.
problems.fix: Note this follows LXX; Hebrew has 'cords' or 'festal procession.'

problems.quote: life-giving Cross
problems.why: The Cross is given many different adjectives across sections; a reader may think these are different objects.
problems.fix: Standardize or note that these are all the same Cross with varied epithets.

variants.text: life-giving wood of the glorious Cross

problems.quote: one now proclaimed in every orthodox church
problems.why: The Nicene Creed's homoousios is rendered differently; reader may miss the connection.
problems.fix: Use 'one in being' consistently or explain the creedal term at first use.

variants.text: one now proclaimed in every orthodox church

problems.quote: Branches, as those skilled in these matters say, are things that have been soiled by neglect or age, and then by care and diligence are adorned again to something more precious, for the gladness and delight of those who will feast at weddings in some other bright celebration.
problems.why: This sentence is nearly incomprehensible; it reads like a word-for-word gloss on a Greek allegorical interpretation.
problems.fix: Rewrite to clarify: the 'branches' symbolize renewed souls, restored for a future heavenly celebration.

problems.quote: something ecstatic with the sacred trumpet
problems.why: 'Ecstatic' is a modern psychological term; the Greek likely means 'inspired utterance' or 'rhapsodic.'
problems.fix: Use 'inspired' or 'rhapsodic' instead of 'ecstatic.'

problems.quote: You have given to those who fear you a sign by which to flee from before the bow
problems.why: Psalm 60:4 (LXX 59:5) in standard texts reads 'a banner' or 'a standard,' not 'a sign by which to flee from before the bow.'

previous_english: For those who are storm-tossed, the Cross is a harbor of perfect calm. For those who are attacked in war, the Cross is a peace that cannot be shaken. The Cross is the boast of boasts for the orthodox, and for heretics a condemnation that never rests. The Cross is the destruction of idolatry and the raising up of true reverence. The Cross is the teacher of virginity and the guardian of self-control. The Cross is the security of the righteous and the repentance of sinners. The Cross is the adornment of monks and the good order of those who live in holiness. The Cross is the protector of infants, the discipline of the young, and the supporting staff of the aged. The Cross is a treasure for the poor that costs nothing, and a teacher of self-sufficiency for the rich. The Cross is the road for those who have wandered, and an unerring guide for those who are perishing. The Cross is rest in the labors of the day, and help in the terrors of the night. The Cross is the good order of the nations, and the deepest calm of the whole world.

And what shall we say, or what shall we pass over, or how shall we praise you, all-glorious Cross? For the King of glory has shown you forth alone from all creation as an unconquered weapon against the devil, and against sin, and against death. Therefore we are all blessed who have been deemed worthy to see the holy day of your exaltation. You are the proclamation of the prophets; for rejoicing in you they sing out daily to God, saying: "You have given to those who fear you a banner by which to flee from before the bow" (Psalm 60:4 (LXX 59:5)). You are the boast of the apostles. For they cry out unceasingly in the holy Church through one of their sacred heralds: "May it never be for me to boast, except in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ" (Galatians 6:14). You are also the crown of the martyrs, since they too took up the Cross and followed the Lord. You are the boast and the joy of those who dwell in mountains and caves and holes in the earth for the name of the Lord, because they too have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. You are refreshment and rest for those near and those far off. O the inexpressible grace of the Master's Cross! O the inexpressible and incomprehensible mysteries in it!

And so that I too, Alexander, may say something inspired with the sacred trumpet: "O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments!" (Romans 11:33). For by the tree of condemnation we were put to death, and by the tree of life we were made alive. Because of the boundless grace of the Master who saved us, we must keep this all-festal feast "among the thick branches, up to the horns of the altar" (Psalm 118:27, LXX 117:27, following the Septuagint). Branches, as biblical interpreters say, are things that have been soiled by neglect or age, and then by care and diligence are adorned again to something more precious, for the gladness and delight of those who will feast at weddings in some other bright celebration. Let us therefore dispose ourselves as we have been instructed, and having stripped off the shame that has come upon our conscience from carelessness, let us celebrate this bright and all-holy day of the memory of the life-giving Cross with acts of mercy and with faith, taking up, as the divine Scripture says, a confidence adorned with reverence, and lifting on our shoulders the victorious weapon of the life-giving Cross, let us cry out to God the angelic hymn given to us from heaven for the ceasing of all wrath, as is our custom: "Holy God, holy mighty, holy immortal, have mercy on us." Holy Trinity, incomprehensible, unbounded, inseparable, one in being, sharing one throne, co-eternal, sharing one glory, have mercy on us, and be merciful to our sins for the sake of your holy name, and grant us to find mercy and compassion on the day of your just recompense. For you are our God, and to you, Father, Son, and Spirit, belong glory, majesty, might, and authority before every age, now and to all the ages of ages. Amen.
